newsitem.title: USA: Kasich doubts large U.S. tax cut possible.
newsitem.headline: Kasich doubts large U.S. tax cut possible.

text.p: House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich said Thursday he doubted it would be possible to enact a five-year tax cut of $190 billion as proposed by Senate Republicans because President Clinton would reject the deep spending cuts that would require.
Speaking to reporters, the Ohio Republican said he felt Congress should first grapple with the difficult problem of curbing federal spending before it considered cutting taxes.
However, he added that he supported the goal of cutting taxes. House Republicans have not proposed a specific size of tax cut and Clinton has requested $100 billion through 2002.

"To begin talking right now about some level of tax cuts without understanding precisely what is going on with this budget is a mistake," Kasich added. He told the panel he would insist both Republicans and Democrats adhere to conservative economic estimates in developing this year's budget.
"If our people, in an effort to get more tax cuts, want to fudge the numbers and pick a more optimistic economic scenario, I am not going to go for it," he said.

"There has been circulating around this town in this era of good feeling this notion that we could just trip and glide our way into balance in 2002. This is going to be excruciatingly difficult," he told reporters after the hearing.
